researched.name: GK Energy Ltd
researched.reason: H1 FY27 revenue Rs 907.85 cr (+38.9% YoY) and PAT Rs 109.04 cr (+30.7%) clear the triage bar, at 8.8x trailing (BSE's own header: EPS 11.04, PE 8.89 standalone; ConEPS 11.17, ConPE 8.78) on a Rs 1,990.7 cr market cap inside the band where 5x runs happen. Published at LOW confidence, because the research produced two things that pull opposite ways and both are in the card. For it: the forward position is unusually well documented for a small cap - Rs 454.50 cr of rooftop (1,00,000 systems of 1 kW at Rs 45,450/kW incl GST, LoE 26-Aug-2026, plus five years of O&M), Rs 330.29 cr of pumps (14,000 off-grid 5 HP systems at Rs 2.36 lakh each incl GST, LoA 23-Oct-2026, 60-day execution), and a 150 MW/300 MWh BESS award at a tariff of Rs 2,38,000 per MW per month = Rs 42.84 cr a year excl GST for 15 years. The two EPC legs are 43.9% of a Rs 1,786.62 cr trailing year, the band the order study found reached 2x 35.7% of the time. Against it, and this is why confidence is low: the quarter that triggered the card is a deceleration, not an acceleration. Q2 revenue +12.3%, EBITDA +0.9%, margin 20.6% -> 18.5%, EPS DOWN Rs 2.70 -> Rs 2.43, revenue -20.3% QoQ. Systems installed rose 41.8% while REVENUE PER SYSTEM FELL 20.8% (Rs 2.62 lakh -> Rs 2.08 lakh), and 21.7% across the half - arithmetic from the company's own two series, and the single number that explains the quarter. The stated order book has fallen for a year on the company's own documents: Rs 1,028.96 cr (15-Aug-2025) -> Rs 863.98 cr (30-Sep-2025) -> Rs 803.24 cr (31-Dec-2025) -> Rs 710 cr (19-May-2026 call) -> Rs 541 cr (Q1 FY27 press release) -> Rs 788 cr today, and today's figure is explicitly mixed-date, 'as on 30.09.2026 and including orders received post September 2026'. Notably the rooftop LoE plus the pump LoA come to Rs 784.79 cr, within Rs 3.21 cr (0.4%) of the stated Rs 788 cr - stated on the card as an arithmetic observation, not a claim about what the figure is. Receivables Rs 586.07 cr -> Rs 1,012.38 cr in six months, debtor days 204 against 140 at FY26, and net cash of Rs 240.62 cr became net debt of Rs 153.78 cr with cash down to Rs 5.05 cr - the whole IPO raise is in receivables, against a deck that still describes the 'transition to a net cash surplus balance sheet position'. The company's own footnote says Rs 377.48 cr was collected after 30-Sep, which would take debtor days back to about 128; recorded as stated and unverified. And measured against our own study, nine order or empanelment filings in 240 days puts this in the serial-filer bucket that reached 2x only 17.3% of the time and NEVER 5x. One more thing a reader should see: the Rs 454.50 cr of new work is PM Surya Ghar household rooftop, the one programme in our measured table that UNDERPERFORMED the market (basket 1.8x against 2.0x, 0 of 9 made 5x), while the pump business sits in PM-KUSUM/Magel Tyala, the 5.5x basket. The order book is rotating from the basket that paid into the one that did not. Also logged: a same-evening corrigendum at 19:34 on an arithmetical rounding-off error in consolidated segment revenue, and a consolidated segment page that is image-only, in which the smaller of two segments falls from Rs 199.70 cr (FY26) to Rs 15.92 cr (H1 FY27) - we could not read the segment names and did not guess them.

researched.name: Remi Edelstahl Tubulars Ltd
researched.reason: The order-wins flag is CONFIRMED and the order is real: Rs 60.25 cr of stainless steel welded and seamless tubes, net of GST, for heat exchangers of thermal power generating equipment, filed 28-Oct-2026, against a stated order book of Rs 108 cr at 31-Mar-2026 - ratio 0.558. On two of the order study's three tests it looks good: the order is 40.1% of a Rs 150.19 cr trailing year (TTM = Q1 FY27 Rs 35.19 cr + FY26 Rs 141.62 cr - Q1 FY26 Rs 26.62 cr), which is the 25-50% band that reached 2x 35.7% of the time, and it is the ONLY order-type filing in the 240 days dossier.py read with a 'complete' read status, i.e. the rare-filer bucket rather than the serial one. NOT PUBLISHED for a reason read out of the company's own presentation: FY26 ALREADY CONTAINED two orders of the same size - 'Rs 62.6 Cr order from a reputed fabricator - high-precision seamless tubes for thermal power plant use' and a 'Rs 57.8 Cr single order - the largest in REMI's history at the time of award' - and FY26 revenue still rose only 2.76% to Rs 142.92 cr, with EBITDA of Rs 9.11 cr (6.4%) and PAT of Rs 2.74 cr. So a Rs 60 cr order is this company's third of the kind in about eighteen months, and the binding constraint is conversion and margin, not order intake. The valuation leaves no room for that: at the Rs 209.90 close BSE's own header gives PE 94.55 and ROE 6.64% on a Rs 282.3 cr market cap, i.e. a 1.9% net margin business at 95x, and median 60-day turnover is Rs 11.1 lakh a day - well under the Rs 25 lakh the playbook treats as the liquidity floor. Even at double FY26's margin the new order adds roughly Rs 2.4 cr of PAT. What would change the answer, and is worth watching: the WSG Co. (South Korea) collaboration for ultra-high-purity, bright-annealed, coil-drawn and titanium welded tubes aimed at semiconductor, biotech and data-centre power markets, where the deck says 'product trials ... are currently in progress' and commercial production is 'expected to commence shortly'; plus nuclear approvals from IGCAR, BHAVINI and NPCIL and supplies to the PFBR reactor and a fuel recycling facility. Those are genuinely high-margin adjacencies, but no revenue, no margin and no date is disclosed for any of them, and the company gives no guidance. Positive housekeeping noted: promoter holding rose from 68.85% at 30-Jun-2026 to 69.54%. Capacity 12,000 MT a year at Tarapur; peak monthly dispatch 580 MT in March 2026.

researched.name: DCW Ltd
researched.reason: The headline looks like growth plus a capital return, and the filing says otherwise. Q2 FY27 revenue Rs 662.86 cr against Rs 539.21 cr, +22.9% YoY and +22.3% QoQ - but Q2 PBT FELL 33.4% to Rs 14.02 cr from Rs 21.05 cr, a 2.1% PBT margin. For the half, revenue Rs 1,204.77 cr (+18.7%) with PBT DOWN 62.9% to Rs 14.38 cr from Rs 38.72 cr. The H1 PAT of Rs 44.91 cr, which looks like +78.2%, is almost entirely a Rs 34.28 cr DEFERRED TAX CREDIT taken in Q1; strip it out and H1 PAT is about Rs 10.6 cr, so the trailing multiple on real earnings is roughly 60-65x on a Rs 1,330.6 cr market cap. Power and fuel alone was Rs 95.66 cr in Q2, 14.4% of revenue. The board did approve a buyback - up to 68,96,551 shares, 2.34% of capital, at a maximum of Rs 58 against the Rs 45.08 close, for up to Rs 40 cr through the open market, with promoters (45.59%) excluded - and a Rs 40 cr buyback at a 28.7% premium cap is a genuine signal of board confidence. It is not enough against a half-year PBT of Rs 14.38 cr. Two unprovided contingencies in the auditor's limited review were also read and weighed: the Sahupuram land repossession, where the Madras High Court has granted an interim stay and 'the determination of cost of land by the revenue authorities is pending'; and income-tax orders following a November-2023 search reducing available MAT credit by Rs 16.94 cr plus a Rs 1.06 cr demand, with 'no provision ... made for the aforesaid demands'. The commodity angle was checked and deliberately not used: DCW makes PVC, caustic soda, soda ash and synthetic iron oxide pigment, and signals.json has caustic soda +3.20 and PVC resin +1.79 up, but both rest on the April-2026 WPI panel, so there is no current price evidence to build a spread case on.

THE PYTHON-INTERPRETER TRAP OF 2026-10-22 RECURRED ON THIS FRESH VM AND WAS FIXED IN-RUN. The routine prompt's step 0 uses `pip install --quiet pymupdf`, but on this VM `pip` is python3.13's (/usr/bin/pip, pip 24.0 from /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages) while the interpreter that runs the builders is python3.11.17 (/usr/local/bin/python3). So pymupdf and xlrd went to an interpreter nothing uses. Consequences measured before the fix: scan.py printed 'SELFTEST FAIL - OCCL 30-Sep-2026 anti-dumping duty raise, generic subject: got []', which silently disables generic-heading TRADE classification - the exact failure the selftest exists to catch - and it wrote 77 EMPTY FILES into the PDF-text cache, which would have poisoned later reads; minsteel.py died outright with ModuleNotFoundError on fitz. Fixed by reinstalling with `python3 -m pip install pymupdf xlrd`, deleting the 77 empty cache entries and re-running: scan.py then printed SELFTEST PASS and found 13 candidates against 10 before. SUGGESTED FIX for the owner: change step 0 of the routine prompt from `pip install` to `python3 -m pip install`, so the packages always land in the interpreter that will import them. Note the ideas-feeds workflow is NOT affected - it uses actions/setup-python and its `pip install -q pymupdf xlrd` resolves to the same 3.11.17.

order_wins.py over-read two order values, both caught by opening the letters (step 4a-iii) and both now recorded in orderwins_verified.json with qualifies=false so they are not re-checked. (a) JUPITER WAGONS (533272): the Rs 1,000 cr 'base order book' is not an order book - the document says the company 'Reiterates its target of a Rs 1,000 crore BESS order book by FY27', a forward-looking target for ONE SEGMENT. The ratio of 1.14 is meaningless; the Rs 1,140 cr win itself (2,583 BOXNHL and BOXNS wagons from the Ministry of Railways) is real. The extractor accepted a segment TARGET phrased with the words 'order book' as a stated order book. (b) ADMACH SYSTEMS (544669): the summed 'win' of Rs 77.42 cr is the company's own restated ORDER BOOK in the order letter ('Our current order book is INR 77.42 Crores (with GST)'); the actual purchase order is 'valued at Rs 115.97 lakhs (with GST)', i.e. Rs 1.16 cr - overstated about 67x, true ratio 0.015. The reading cross-checks: Rs 76.25 cr of prior book plus a Rs 1.16 cr order gives exactly the Rs 77.42 cr the letter states. BOTH are the same class of bug - an order-book sentence inside an order letter being taken as the order value - and a rule that rejects a candidate value appearing in the same sentence as 'our current order book' / 'order book stands at' would catch both.
